jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
BoomerangFX

Location:
Mississauga, Ontario — on-site, five days per week
Reports to:
Chief Executive Officer

Mandatory Experience

A Canadian CPA designation and hands-on experience leading finance and operations for a PE-backed SaaS company scaling ARR from $5 million to $50 million.

Why Join BoomerangFX?

BoomerangFX is a global healthcare technology company bringing SaaS, artificial intelligence and digital marketing together to help private-pay healthcare practices operate and grow. Recognized through Deloitte’s Technology Fast 500 program, we are building technology that simplifies practice management, strengthens patient engagement and helps healthcare businesses reach more people.
With operations in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia and India
, we are scaling internationally and working at the forefront of AI in healthcare. Our teams collaborate across countries and disciplines to turn new ideas into products and services that make a practical difference for customers.

Joining BoomerangFX is an opportunity to build your career alongside a growing global business. You will have meaningful responsibility, exposure to international markets and the opportunity to contribute ideas, develop your skills and see the impact of your work. We welcome people who take ownership, move quickly and want to help build what comes next.

The Role

Reporting to the CEO, you will lead financial management and general operations with strong financial acumen, commercial judgment and a practical approach to execution
.

You will oversee the Controller and Accountant
while taking responsibility for talent acquisition, human resources, vendor negotiations and corporate infrastructure
. You must be comfortable reviewing the detail, challenging assumptions and resolving issues personally while building an accountable team.

Financial Leadership and Accounting Oversight

Directly oversee the Controller and Accountant, setting clear expectations for accuracy, reporting deadlines, financial controls and accountability. Review their work and provide hands-on guidance on complex issues.
Own the quality and timeliness of monthly, quarterly and annual financial reporting. Review financial statements, balance-sheet reconciliations, management reports and material accounting judgments.
Oversee billing, subscription revenue recognition, deferred revenue, collections, accounts payable, payroll and intercompany reporting. Maintain clear controls over approvals, payments and financial records.
Coordinate external accountants, auditors and tax advisers, and strengthen accounting policies and controls as the company scales.

Financial Performance and Cash Management

Lead annual budgeting, rolling forecasts, financial modelling and variance analysis. Challenge assumptions and translate financial results into clear recommendations for the CEO and department leaders.
Own a rolling 13-week cash-flow forecast and longer-term liquidity projections. Improve collections, working capital, spending discipline and visibility into financial commitments.
Analyze profitability by product, service and market. Use SaaS metrics, including ARR, retention, churn, gross margin, customer acquisition cost and payback, to evaluate performance and investment decisions.
Assess hiring plans, pricing, operating costs and major expenditures against expected returns. Drive measurable improvements in margins, productivity and progress toward sustainable profitability.

Talent Acquisition and Human Resources

Oversee talent acquisition and human resources, including internal staff and external providers. Align recruitment priorities and headcount plans with approved budgets and business needs.
Oversee recruitment execution, agency relationships, hiring timelines, onboarding and workforce planning. Hold hiring managers accountable for clear requirements, timely decisions and hiring outcomes.
Oversee HR administration, employee records, compensation and benefits coordination, performance-review processes, employee relations and offboarding, working with qualified advisers where required.

Vendor Negotiations and Corporate Infrastructure

Lead vendor negotiations and oversee procurement, contracts and renewals. Secure commercially sound pricing, payment terms and service commitments, and hold providers accountable for delivery.
Oversee corporate infrastructure, including offices, facilities, equipment, business systems and outsourced services. Ensure these resources support reliable daily operations and future growth.
Work with technology leaders on corporate IT providers, software licences, infrastructure spending and business continuity arrangements. Improve utilization and eliminate unnecessary or duplicate costs.

Operating Performance and Team Leadership

Establish operating KPIs, management dashboards and regular performance reviews across finance and the functions under your oversight.
Improve workflows, approval processes and reporting through practical automation and stronger data quality. Ensure corrective actions have accountable owners and deadlines.
Lead and develop the finance team and collaborate with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Product and Technology leaders to improve execution and resource allocation.

Mandatory Qualifications

CPA designation in good standing in Canada.

At least 5-7 years of progressive finance experience, including hands-on leadership across financial reporting, controllership, budgeting, forecasting, cash management and operating performance.
At least three years of hands-on experience in a fast-paced SaaS business, including leadership of finance and operations for a PE-backed SaaS company scaling ARR from $5 million to $50 million.

Strong financial acumen and commercial judgment: the ability to interrogate financial results, build credible forecasts, evaluate SaaS unit economics and make sound decisions on costs, headcount and investment.
Proven experience directly supervising a Controller and accounting staff, reviewing their work and maintaining high standards for financial accuracy, control and delivery.
Direct experience overseeing talent acquisition, human resources, vendor negotiations and corporate infrastructure, with accountability for operational results.
Advanced financial modelling and Excel or Google Sheets skills, proficiency with accounting and reporting systems, and the ability to explain financial issues clearly to business leaders.
A record of personal ownership and effective execution in an environment with rapidly changing priorities, tight deadlines and limited resources. You must be willing to work on-site in Mississauga five days per week.

Additional Experience We Value

Measurable success improving profitability, cash generation or progress toward break-even.
Experience managing multiple entities, currencies or international operations.
Experience in healthcare technology or a business combining SaaS subscriptions and services.
Experience implementing finance systems, automating reporting or supporting transaction readiness.

Compensation and Benefits

Base salary:
CAD $135,000–$150,000 annually.
Annual target performance bonus:
50% of base salary, based on achievement of agreed performance objectives.
Total target compensation:
CAD $202,500–$225,000 annually.
Performance objectives will reflect measurable outcomes in profitability, cash management, financial reporting and operational execution.
Comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage.
Paid vacation and free on-site parking.
An opportunity to work closely with the CEO and senior leadership and make a measurable contribution to a growing global healthcare technology business.

How to Apply

Submit your résumé with a brief summary of your experience in high-growth software or technology-enabled companies, including two or three measurable financial or operational results you personally delivered.
Shortlisted candidates should be prepared to discuss their experience with financial oversight, operational leadership, strategic planning, and board reporting. CPA credentials, employment experience, and professional references will be verified.

Accessibility Statement

BoomerangFX is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals and are dedicated to accommodating people with disabilities. If you require accommodation at any stage of the application process, please contact recruitment@boomerangfx.com.

jobs.title: Director, Data Solutions Architect
jobs.description:
Location

Brookfield Place - 181 Bay Street

Technology Services

Technology Services (TS) is responsible for delivering all enterprise infrastructure, applications and related end user technology services across all Brookfield business groups.

Brookfield Culture

Brookfield has a unique and dynamic culture. We seek team members who have a long-term focus and whose values align with our Attributes of a Brookfield Leader: Entrepreneurial, Collaborative and Disciplined. Brookfield is committed to the development of our people through challenging work assignments and exposure to diverse businesses.

Job Description

Role Summary

Leads the design of business-aligned data solutions that translate strategic priorities and product needs into scalable, governed architecture patterns. This role partners closely with business, product, engineering, and architecture stakeholders to assess requirements, define end-to-end solution designs, and ensure data capabilities support operational, analytical, and AI use cases. The role is accountable for connecting business intent to practical architecture decisions while maintaining alignment with enterprise standards, controls, and platform strategy.

Key Responsibilities

Assess business priorities, product requirements, and data needs to define solution architecture approaches.
Translate business use cases into end-to-end data solution designs spanning source systems, integration, storage, consumption, and controls.
Partner with product owners, business stakeholders, data architects, and engineering teams to align solution designs to enterprise standards and delivery priorities.
Define target-state architecture patterns, integration approaches, and data flows for reporting, operational, and AI-enabled use cases.
Lead architecture decisions for new initiatives, enhancements, and platform adoption across business functions.
Ensure solution designs address scalability, resiliency, security, data quality, and governance requirements.
Support prioritization and roadmap planning by evaluating design options, dependencies, trade-offs, and implementation feasibility.
Review proposed solutions and delivery plans to ensure alignment with enterprise architecture, product intent, and business outcomes.
Drive consistency in solution design practices, documentation standards, and architecture governance across regions and teams.
Provide technical leadership and guidance to engineering teams during delivery to ensure architectural integrity.

Required Experience

10+ years of experience in data, solution architecture, enterprise architecture, or related technology roles.
Experience designing end-to-end data solutions in complex enterprise environments.
Experience working with business stakeholders to assess requirements, define target-state solutions, and support delivery execution.
Experience in financial services, asset management, or similarly regulated and complex industries.
Experience with enterprise data platforms, integration patterns, reporting ecosystems, and governed data environments.

Skills & Qualifications

Technical knowledge and systems expertise: Strong understanding of enterprise data architecture, integration patterns, data platforms, reporting ecosystems, and the architecture foundations required to support analytics, AI, and operational use cases.
Analytical and problem-solving skills: Ability to assess business needs, evaluate design options, and translate complex requirements into scalable and governed solution architectures.
Communication and collaboration capabilities: Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and cross-functional influence skills, with the ability to connect business intent to technical design decisions.
Ability to work in cross-functional or global teams: Experience operating across global teams and coordinating with business, product, architecture, engineering, and governance stakeholders.
Understanding of technology governance, security, or operational practices: Strong understanding of data governance, security, risk management, compliance, and operational standards, with experience embedding them into solution design.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting cloud-based data modernization initiatives and enterprise platform transformations.
Experience designing data solutions that support self-service analytics, advanced analytics, or AI-enabled use cases.
Familiarity with asset management, investment, portfolio, finance, or operational data domains.
Experience establishing reusable architecture patterns, reference designs, and solution governance practices.

Salary Range: $150,000 - $185,000 CAD

Position Opening Reason:

New Position

Brookfield is committed to creating an accessible and inclusive organization. We are committed to providing barrier-free and accessible employment practices in compliance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act. Recursive focuses on building self-improving superintelligent systems to automate knowledge discovery across complex domains. The organization is driven by a mission to accelerate scientific and technological progress through advanced AI. Team members collaborate across disciplines to design tools that transform how information is analyzed, synthesized, and applied. Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in a remote, distributed team.

jobs.title: Technology and Innovation - Associate Director (NetSuite)
jobs.description:
Riveron is looking for an Associate Director to join our Technology and Innovation practice. This client facing role will interact with key leadership (CFO, Controller, etc.) and will contribute to the areas of business development and sales, practice development, and project execution.

As an Associate Director, you will lead the delivery of client engagements, serving as the day-to-day point of contact for the client, guiding a team of consultants through the project lifecycle, and ensuring that high quality projects are consistently executed on time and on budget. While developing your project and people management skills, you will further augment your advisory toolkit by digging deep into client problems in real-time and delivering ongoing thought partnership. With business leaders to guide you along the way – including a dedicated performance advisor – you will contribute to developing the practice as we continue to invest in accelerating your growth.

Who You Are

Bachelor’s degree, preferably in Accounting, Finance, or Management Information Systems (MIS)
7+ years of implementation or optimization experience and should have prior experience with architecting ERP solutions on NetSuite.
Leading or supporting full-cycle NetSuite Implementations
Previous experience and ability to gather business requirements and effectively implement an ERP, CRM, & PSA solution
Mastery of Microsoft Office Products.
Consulting experience in other business applications including QuickBooks, Intacct, Salesforce.com, Microsoft Dynamics, Oracle, SAP, and/or PeopleSoft is a plus.
Software as a Service (SaaS) or Cloud experience is a plus.
Certified NetSuite ERP consultant is a plus.
Ability to develop, grow and sustain client relationships.
Entrepreneurial spirit and a solution-oriented mindset
Ability to work in ever-changing, dynamic environments.
Ability to craft and deliver verbal, written, and oral messages and make recommendations to a variety of audiences, including client leadership and internal teams.
Desire to get involved in the Riveron culture and internal initiatives, including community service, training, interviewing, intramurals, and other social/networking activities.
Passionate about best practices and the ability to challenge the need for customization and not just using standard native functionality by configuring the platform.

What You'll Do

Execute Projects

Collaborate with Implementation team members to develop effective and scalable NetSuite solutions. Leverage best practices wherever possible.
Work directly with Implementation team members to develop business requirements and translate requirements into specific NetSuite functionality.
Lead client workshops to define implementation strategy to support the growth of the business requirements.
Lead and/or support implementation team(s) in solution design and work with the implementation team to implement the solution.
Work with client IT teams to ensure that the solution design is well understood by the client. Should be comfortable presenting the solution design to the external and internal teams.
Ensure completion of tasks, milestones, and components including but not limited to functional specifications, design specifications, configurations, quality assurance, implementations and project reviews for engagements.
Define integration requirements and collaborate with integration team to interface other outside applications with NetSuite.
Oversee and lead engagement teams through all phases of a NetSuite ERP implementation or optimization project including business process design, configuration, user acceptance testing, training, cutover and go-live stabilization.

Support Business Development and Sales

Identify expansion opportunities on client engagements to cross-sell Riveron’s services
Participate in pre-sales meetings with current and prospective clients to assess project level-of-effort and to assist in determining in NetSuite is the best fit for requirements presented.
Identify the NetSuite modules and determine the timeline, resource plan, level-of-effort and fee estimates required for implementation in achieving client objectives.

NetSuite Practice Development

Work with practice leadership to develop and deliver NetSuite-specific training, business development training and collateral and engagement materials/templates.

Applications for this evergreen opportunity will be accepted through Dec 31, 2026.

At Riveron, we partner with clients—from global multinationals to high-growth private entities—to solve complex finance challenges, guided by our DELTA values: Drive, Excellence, Leadership, Teamwork, and Accountability. Our entrepreneurial culture thrives on collaboration, diverse perspectives, and delivering exceptional outcomes. We are committed to fostering growth, both for our clients and our people, through mentorship, integrity, and a client-centric approach. This inclusive environment offers flexibility, progressive benefits, and meaningful opportunities for impactful work that supports well-being in and out of the office.

jobs.title: Director of FP&A
jobs.description:
Company Background

Our client is North America’s largest lawn care franchisor, serving more than 800,000 households across approximately 1,000 territories across a majority of U.S. states and Canadian provinces. The group combines a franchise network with substantial company-owned operations and provides lawn care services and mosquito/tick control.

The business has moved from a founder-led environment to a private equity-backed one while continuing to be led by its existing management team. To support this next stage, finance is undertaking two major initiatives: modernizing its infrastructure, tools and ERP systems, and establishing a consistent monthly reporting cadence for private equity investors and the Board of Directors.

Role Overview

Reporting to the CFO, this role will lead consolidated reporting of actual results, budgets and future forecasts across the group. The immediate priority is to own Board, executive and lender reporting, working closely with accounting and business leaders and taking ownership of the tools and processes developed an in process 100 day plan engagement to lay foundations for reporting. Over the next 24 months, the role will also play a significant part in finance transformation, particularly initiatives affecting reporting and FP&A.

This is a player-coach role. At the company's current size, the leader of FP&A must be hands-on, building the models, reporting packages and processes personally, while also setting the standard for how the business thinks about financial performance. The successful candidate will be expected to develop a strong financial culture across the organization, partnering with operators to build their financial acumen and equip them to manage the business through its next phase of growth.
On an ongoing basis, the successful candidate will serve as a key finance partner to the CFO and operating leaders. As the business grows and its needs evolve, the successful candidate will build the FP&A function, including its team, responsibilities and recurring planning and reporting cadence.

Role & Responsiblities

Management and Board Reporting
Own consolidated and business-level reporting across franchising and corporate operations in Canada and the US in a timely manner, including visibility of bank accounts and cash balances across entities and currencies.
Align with the CFO, executive team and PE fund on reporting needs, key metrics and presentation.
Develop a recurring reporting package covering financial performance, operational KPIs, budget variances and management commentary.
Translate results into clear insights, risks and recommended actions.

Budgeting, Forecasting and Financial Modeling
Streamline and lead the annual budget, rolling forecast and long-range planning processes with the respective business teams and consolidate the results for Board/Executive reporting.
Build and maintain an integrated three-statement financial model (by business stream; as well as consolidated) covering the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow.
Ensure driver-based budgeting linked to operational KPIs and business priorities.
Partner with business leaders to challenge assumptions, assess resource needs and improve forecast accuracy, building their ownership of the numbers.
Develop scenario and sensitivity analyses to support strategic and operating decisions.
Own a rolling 13-week cash forecast and longer-term liquidity projections.

Business Performance and Profitability Analysis
Establish consistent financial and operational KPIs across business units and help operators understand and act on them.
Use the integrated financial model to analyze profitability by business stream, entity, branch and geography, as appropriate.
Assess revenue growth, margins, labour productivity, overhead and cost allocations.
Identify opportunities to improve profitability and track delivery against agreed initiatives.

Lender Reporting and Covenant Monitoring
Develop and own the recurring lender reporting package, including covenant calculation templates and supporting schedules.
Establish reliable data sources, review procedures and accountability for timely submissions.
Forecast covenant compliance and available headroom, flagging potential constraints early.
Identify challenges or gaps affecting delivery of lender reporting and implement practical recommendations.
Partner with accounting and operations to improve working capital and cash conversion.

Finance Transformation and Automation
Play a significant role in the 24-month finance transformation roadmap, helping rebuild the finance function through modern technology, improved processes and automation.
Lead one or more transformation workstreams affecting reporting and FP&A, including budgeting, forecasting and financial analysis.
Partner with accounting, IT and business leaders to evaluate and implement planning, reporting, consolidation and business intelligence tools.
Define FP&A requirements for the future ERP and related systems, including data structures, reporting dimensions and integration needs.

Culture and Business Partnership
Lead by example, personally building and owning the core models, reports and analyses while setting the standards and habits that raise the bar for the finance function.
Develop a financial culture grounded in accountability, data-driven decision-making and a shared understanding of what drives profitability, cash flow and growth.
Build financial acumen among operators through coaching, training and accessible tools, helping them read their own P&Ls, KPIs and budget variances and take ownership of results.
Mentor and develop the future FP&A team, defining roles, standards and career paths as the function grows.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics or a related field; CPA, CA, CFA or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive FP&A, corporate finance or finance leadership experience, ideally in a private equity-backed, multi-entity or multi-location service business.
Proven experience owning Board, investor and lender reporting, including covenant monitoring and compliance forecasting.
Advanced financial modeling skills, including integrated three-statement models, driver-based budgets and scenario and sensitivity analyses.
Hands-on experience with ERP, planning and business intelligence tools, and a track record of automating reporting and improving finance processes.
Demonstrated ability to coach and influence non-finance leaders, building financial acumen and accountability across operating teams.
Strong communicator who can present to a Board and private equity sponsor and translate complex results into clear, actionable insights.
A hands-on, player-coach mindset: comfortable building the work personally while developing a team and a finance culture.
Experience in franchise, seasonal or cross-border (Canada and U.S.) businesses is an asset.

jobs.title: Director of Portfolio Finance
jobs.description:
The opportunity

We are building a centralized finance function for our portfolio, and we are looking for the person to lead it. You will give Rhyno greater control over cash, faster and more reliable reporting, and the financial credibility to work with lenders and financing partners from a position of strength.
This role suits someone who is comfortable deep in the numbers and equally comfortable stepping back to tell the partners clearly what they see: where each business stands, what healthy looks like, and how far there is to go.

What you will do

1. Treasury and liquidity

Own rolling 13-week cash flow forecasts across all six companies, refreshed weekly with variance analysis against actuals.
Build the 12 to 24 month liquidity outlook that feeds budgets and planning.
Manage AP prioritization and supplier payment plans and monitor bank accounts and cash daily.
Track available credit and covenant headroom under base and downside cases and flag liquidity risks early.
Manage banking relationships, account structures and intercompany funding across the portfolio.

2. Financial reporting
Accelerate month-end and annual financial reporting across the portfolio.
Improve consolidation, and set a common reporting template, chart of accounts mapping and reporting calendar for every company.
Produce a weekly liquidity view and a monthly reporting package for Rhyno leadership.
Set the cadence and content of financial reporting for board meetings.
Coordinate year-end audits with external auditors.

3. Budgeting and forecasting
Lead the annual budget for each company and for the consolidated portfolio.
Run rolling forecasts and monthly variance analysis and hold company leaders accountable to plan.
Benchmark each company's P&L against a healthy business in its space and set clear targets for where it should be.

4. Operational advisory
Identify cash flow inefficiencies across receivables, payables and inventory, and set working capital targets with each company.
Tie project billing (schedules of billings, progress draws and holdbacks) to cash so invoicing moves on time.
Advise leadership on operational resizing and cost reductions.
Find quick wins across the portfolio in financial systems, operations and management practices.
Strengthen financial controls, including payment approvals, signing authority and fraud prevention.
Step in hands-on when a company is under cash pressure, and coach company finance teams on cash discipline.

5. Lender readiness
Produce accurate, consistent, lender-ready reporting that shows forecasting reliability, financial control and management accountability.
Prepare covenant calculations, borrowing base certificates and lender reporting.
Lead responses to lender and auditor requests.
Support credit renewals, amendments and financing discussions alongside Rhyno leadership.

How success is measured
Weekly cash forecast accuracy within agreed tolerance across the portfolio.
Faster, more reliable month-end and year-end reporting.
Cash released through working capital improvement against target.
No covenant breaches or liquidity surprises.
On-time, credible reporting to the board and lenders.
Continuous improvement in systems and processes across every portfolio finance department, with each company's finance lead supported in driving their own improvements.

What you bring
CPA with 5 to 10+ years of relevant experience.
Background in PE-backed manufacturing, multi-entity finance or corporate restructuring.
Hands-on experience with refinancing, liquidity management and financial reporting.
Strong operational understanding, beyond accounting or FP&A alone.
Experience as a Finance Director, Divisional CFO or Senior Finance Manager in a $50M to $300M manufacturing business, or in a restructuring or advisory practice.
Ability to shift priorities quickly and move with speed, without compromising accuracy or momentum.
Autonomy and confidence to make decisions with the information available and bring strong, clear recommendations to the partners and board.
An owner’s approach to results, with hands-on accountability from building the model to presenting the findings.
A continuous improvement approach, with the curiosity to test the numbers, dig into root causes and bring structure where there isn’t any.
Ability to build trust with company leaders and finance teams through clear, direct communication, high integrity and composure under pressure.

Compensation
Base salary of $160,000 to $190,000, plus performance bonus and benefits.
How to apply
Please send your resume to Michelle McDonald, Head of Talent, Rhyno Equity Group.
This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Rhyno Equity Group is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and are committed to a hiring process free from discrimination, in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code.

Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process, in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). Please let us know if you require an accommodation.

new_jobs.title: Director of FP&A
new_jobs.description:
Company Background

Our client is North America’s largest lawn care franchisor, serving more than 800,000 households across approximately 1,000 territories across a majority of U.S. states and Canadian provinces. The group combines a franchise network with substantial company-owned operations and provides lawn care services and mosquito/tick control.

The business has moved from a founder-led environment to a private equity-backed one while continuing to be led by its existing management team. To support this next stage, finance is undertaking two major initiatives: modernizing its infrastructure, tools and ERP systems, and establishing a consistent monthly reporting cadence for private equity investors and the Board of Directors.

Role Overview

Reporting to the CFO, this role will lead consolidated reporting of actual results, budgets and future forecasts across the group. The immediate priority is to own Board, executive and lender reporting, working closely with accounting and business leaders and taking ownership of the tools and processes developed an in process 100 day plan engagement to lay foundations for reporting. Over the next 24 months, the role will also play a significant part in finance transformation, particularly initiatives affecting reporting and FP&A.

This is a player-coach role. At the company's current size, the leader of FP&A must be hands-on, building the models, reporting packages and processes personally, while also setting the standard for how the business thinks about financial performance. The successful candidate will be expected to develop a strong financial culture across the organization, partnering with operators to build their financial acumen and equip them to manage the business through its next phase of growth.
On an ongoing basis, the successful candidate will serve as a key finance partner to the CFO and operating leaders. As the business grows and its needs evolve, the successful candidate will build the FP&A function, including its team, responsibilities and recurring planning and reporting cadence.

Role & Responsiblities

Management and Board Reporting
Own consolidated and business-level reporting across franchising and corporate operations in Canada and the US in a timely manner, including visibility of bank accounts and cash balances across entities and currencies.
Align with the CFO, executive team and PE fund on reporting needs, key metrics and presentation.
Develop a recurring reporting package covering financial performance, operational KPIs, budget variances and management commentary.
Translate results into clear insights, risks and recommended actions.

Budgeting, Forecasting and Financial Modeling
Streamline and lead the annual budget, rolling forecast and long-range planning processes with the respective business teams and consolidate the results for Board/Executive reporting.
Build and maintain an integrated three-statement financial model (by business stream; as well as consolidated) covering the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow.
Ensure driver-based budgeting linked to operational KPIs and business priorities.
Partner with business leaders to challenge assumptions, assess resource needs and improve forecast accuracy, building their ownership of the numbers.
Develop scenario and sensitivity analyses to support strategic and operating decisions.
Own a rolling 13-week cash forecast and longer-term liquidity projections.

Business Performance and Profitability Analysis
Establish consistent financial and operational KPIs across business units and help operators understand and act on them.
Use the integrated financial model to analyze profitability by business stream, entity, branch and geography, as appropriate.
Assess revenue growth, margins, labour productivity, overhead and cost allocations.
Identify opportunities to improve profitability and track delivery against agreed initiatives.

Lender Reporting and Covenant Monitoring
Develop and own the recurring lender reporting package, including covenant calculation templates and supporting schedules.
Establish reliable data sources, review procedures and accountability for timely submissions.
Forecast covenant compliance and available headroom, flagging potential constraints early.
Identify challenges or gaps affecting delivery of lender reporting and implement practical recommendations.
Partner with accounting and operations to improve working capital and cash conversion.

Finance Transformation and Automation
Play a significant role in the 24-month finance transformation roadmap, helping rebuild the finance function through modern technology, improved processes and automation.
Lead one or more transformation workstreams affecting reporting and FP&A, including budgeting, forecasting and financial analysis.
Partner with accounting, IT and business leaders to evaluate and implement planning, reporting, consolidation and business intelligence tools.
Define FP&A requirements for the future ERP and related systems, including data structures, reporting dimensions and integration needs.

Culture and Business Partnership
Lead by example, personally building and owning the core models, reports and analyses while setting the standards and habits that raise the bar for the finance function.
Develop a financial culture grounded in accountability, data-driven decision-making and a shared understanding of what drives profitability, cash flow and growth.
Build financial acumen among operators through coaching, training and accessible tools, helping them read their own P&Ls, KPIs and budget variances and take ownership of results.
Mentor and develop the future FP&A team, defining roles, standards and career paths as the function grows.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics or a related field; CPA, CA, CFA or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive FP&A, corporate finance or finance leadership experience, ideally in a private equity-backed, multi-entity or multi-location service business.
Proven experience owning Board, investor and lender reporting, including covenant monitoring and compliance forecasting.
Advanced financial modeling skills, including integrated three-statement models, driver-based budgets and scenario and sensitivity analyses.
Hands-on experience with ERP, planning and business intelligence tools, and a track record of automating reporting and improving finance processes.
Demonstrated ability to coach and influence non-finance leaders, building financial acumen and accountability across operating teams.
Strong communicator who can present to a Board and private equity sponsor and translate complex results into clear, actionable insights.
A hands-on, player-coach mindset: comfortable building the work personally while developing a team and a finance culture.
Experience in franchise, seasonal or cross-border (Canada and U.S.) businesses is an asset.
